title: terraform: refactor private GPU node pools, IAM roles and networking state layout
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: Private deployments have accumulated incremental layout choices for GPU node pools, IAM roles, and networking modules which made state management brittle for customer upgrades. Motivation: Unify TF module state layout so upgrades between older private-installer versions and new on-prem bundles are automated and predictable. This PR refactors module boundaries, standardizes remote state layout, and adds explicit state migration helpers. Changes: 1) Consolidate GPU node pool resources into modules/private_gpu/node_pool with clearer inputs for instance_type, accelerators, and node taints. 2) Extract IAM role and policy attachments into modules/private_iam/roles and provide a namespaced resource prefix to avoid collisions on multi-tenant installs. 3) Rework networking state layout: move subnets and route tables to modules/private_networking/vpc to decouple from earlier mixed-module ownership. 4) Add a top-level state-layout.tf which documents remote state key prefixes and exposes expected terraform state mv commands. 5) Provide a migration script (scripts/tf_state_migrate.sh) and documentation to run dry-run and apply phases. 6) Update examples and test harness entries for the private installer and helm charts that reference module paths. Compatibility: default module inputs preserve existing default values, and we provide state migration helpers to move existing resources without resource recreation. Linear tickets: ENG-1423 covers migration automation and INFRA-78 tracks the module boundary changes across repos. Checklist: - [x] Module refactor and unit tests - [x] State migration script and docs - [x] Example private deployment updated - [x] CI/Terraform plan validation passes - [x] Reviewed and approved by infra owners Rollout: Merge gated by migration verification. Operators should run scripts/tf_state_migrate.sh against a staging remote state and verify plan shows no resource replacements before running against production. Follow the migration_plan in this PR for step-by-step commands.

release_notes: Refactor private Terraform modules: GPU node pools, IAM roles, and networking state layout. Add state migration helpers and updated examples. Operators should run provided migration script before upgrading production private deployments.
migration_plan: 1) Checkout branch and read README-private-module-upgrades.md. 2) Run scripts/tf_state_migrate.sh --dry-run against staging remote state to generate terraform state mv commands and a plan. 3) Review plan to confirm no resource replacements. 4) Run scripts/tf_state_migrate.sh --apply to move state keys. 5) Run terraform init && terraform plan && terraform apply in the usual module root for staging. 6) Repeat steps in production during a maintenance window. Notes: The script supports S3/GCS backends and prints a reversible mapping file. Keep backups of remote state before applying.
testing_summary: Added terratest case test/terratest/private_install_test.go to validate module refs and IAM bindings. CI runs terraform validate/plan and an integration smoke test that deploys a minimal private installer to a short-lived cluster. Migration script was exercised against a copied staging state with zero resource replacements in plan. Manual verification done on two internal staging clusters.
notes_for_ops: Run migration in a controlled maintenance window. Back up remote state (s3/gcs) and verify dry-run output. For clusters with live traffic, validate canary routes and fallback policies in Redwood Console before swapping production state. Contact infra-oncall if plan shows resource recreation.
